data_notes: Neither card prints course descriptions, credit values, semester information or prerequisites in any systematic way, so those fields are null, inferred or drawn only from parenthetical notes.

The two cards use the same footnote symbols with different meanings. On the grade 9 card '***' means teacher approval and/or an application; on the grades 10-12 card '***' means an unweighted GPA of 3.0 plus college readiness scores, and '*' alone means teacher approval. Markers are therefore stored per source rather than globally.
The grade 9 card prints a bare '*' beside Algebra 1 Honors, Geometry Honors and 'Algebra 1 Honors* ***' without defining that symbol in its legend.
Algebra 2 Honors is 12003401 on the grade 9 card and 12003400 on the grades 10-12 card. Both are kept as separate entries because the printed numbers differ.
STEM: Robotics 1 Honors is 2002340R on the grade 9 card while STEM: Robotics I Honors is 94101100 on the grades 10-12 card. Both are kept as printed.

The grade 9 card lists 'Theatrical Direction & Stage Management' and 'Stage Management/Directing' as separate lines sharing course number 04005000; they are merged into one entry with a title variant.
AP European History appears twice on the grades 10-12 card under two numbers: 21098300 under Social Studies with World History credit, and 21093800 under Academic Electives. Both are kept.

'Beginning Band' (grade 9 card) and 'Instrumental Ensemble I' (grades 10-12 card) share number 13024600, as do 'Color Guard/Dance' and 'Dance/Color Guard I' at 13053000; each pair is merged with a title variant.
FIU Dual Beginning Drawing / Beginning Painting is printed as 'ART2300/ARC2300'; ARC2300 is an architecture prefix and is likely a typo.

`meets_practical_fine_arts` is set for every course under the arts headings, and additionally for the debate sequence and the career and technical courses, because the graduation chart's line reads "Fine or Performing Arts, Speech, Debate, or eligible Practical Arts". Neither card certifies this course by course, and the chart does not enumerate which practical arts are eligible, so the career and technical courses are a best guess. `meets_pe_requirement` is set for every course under physical education, following the cards' own PE section labels.
Grade levels are the card each course was printed on unless the title narrows them, e.g. 'AP Calculus AB (11th-12th)'.

COHORT MISMATCH: the graduation requirements chart supplied covers students entering grade 9 in the 2013-2014 through 2020-2021 school years. The course cards are for 2026-2027, whose grade 9 students enter well after that window, and whose grades 10-12 students entered in 2024-2026. No cohort on these cards is governed by this chart. It still describes the shape of a Florida diploma accurately, but specific assessment references are out of date: the FSA has been replaced by the B.E.S.T./FAST assessments, and later cohorts carry a separate financial literacy credit requirement, which is why the grade 9 card flags Financial Literacy for students taking AP Human Geography instead. Treat `graduation_requirements` as a best-effort placeholder until the chart for the current cohort is supplied.

Prerequisite links are almost entirely inferred. The cards print a prerequisite for only about a dozen courses; every other edge in the graph was read off a numbered sequence (Spanish II follows Spanish I, Culinary Arts 2 follows Culinary Arts 1) or from the blanket rule that Pre-AICE Physical Education is the prerequisite for all other PE courses. `prerequisites.basis` records which is which; only edges marked 'printed' are attested by a source.

Requirement links are inferred by department and title, not printed. The chart names subjects, not course numbers, so for example every English department course is listed as satisfying the 4.0 English credit line even though a student obviously cannot count all of them. `satisfying_course_codes` means 'may count toward', not 'is sufficient for'.
Westhaven pairs U.S. Government with Economics in single year-long courses, so the same four course codes satisfy both half-credit social studies lines.

Band II (Double Block) is keyed on 13023700 rather than its first printed period code 12023100, which is the AP Calculus AB number and appears to be a typo for 13023100. In the 2.0 build the shared number silently merged Band II into AP Calculus AB; both are now separate entries.

`eoc_course` was set on Algebra 1, Geometry, Biology, U.S. History and the paired Government/Economics courses from the chart's assessment lines. Only Algebra 1, Geometry and Biology are marked with the '#' EOC symbol on the grade 9 card.
'Journalism 1' (1006300A, grade 9 card) and 'Journalism I' (82030000, grades 10-12 card) are kept as separate entries because the printed numbers differ, but they are very likely the same course.

The AICE pathway groups print four course names that do not match the catalog titles (AICE Math (Pre-Calculus), AICE Environmental Mgmt., AICE U.S. History, AICE International World History); each is recorded as a `title_variants` entry on the course it names. Two further lines, AICE Spanish Language and AICE English General Paper, name one syllabus that Westhaven enrols as two courses, so the group lists both.

`graduation_requirements.credits_by_subject` is the 24-credit standard diploma flattened by subject. Each row carries `requirement_ids` pointing back at the chart lines it rolls up, and every course carries `satisfies_requirement_ids`, so a finer count can be made from the same data without re-reading the chart.

The Cambridge AICE Diploma rules in `program_groupings[].diploma_requirements` were taken from Cambridge Assessment International Education on 2026-08-22, not from either course card. They describe the qualification in general; they say nothing about which of Westhaven's courses are entered for which syllabus.

Where a course lists more than one prerequisite, most are one course and its honours or double-block twin, or two routes to the same place (AP Pre-Calculus or AICE Pre-Calculus before AP Calculus AB). Those carry `prerequisites.choice: true`. The physical education sequences are not flagged: the card prints no prerequisite text, and whether Team Sports II wants Team Sports I *or* HOPE, or both, cannot be read off it. An unflagged line over-warns; a wrongly flagged one would let an unmet prerequisite pass in silence.
